title: What If a Star Exploded 50 Light-Years From Earth?

scenes.text: What if a star exploded 50 light-years away? You wouldn't feel a thing, and that's the danger.
Years ago, scientists thought the deadly range was about 25 light-years.
A newer estimate pushes it to roughly 40 to 50 light-years, with no hard cutoff.
The danger is cosmic rays, which boost ionization in the atmosphere, and may raise cancer rates and wildfires.
A blast 150 light-years away, about 2.6 million years ago, may have left a mark on Earth.
The closest candidate, Betelgeuse, sits about 600 light-years away, safely out of range.
